title: Minimum dimension for skew two-planes
notes: The convention for skew planes is unstated.
statement: Disjoint nonparallel affine two-planes first occur in dimension four. Requiring disjoint direction spaces raises the minimum to five. Disjoint projective two-planes require projective dimension five.
reconstruction: \ours{} In dimension four use span(e1,e2) and e4+span(e1,e3). Transverse directions require a translation outside their four-dimensional sum; projective planes correspond to disjoint three-dimensional vector spaces.
fate: Elementary dimension arguments settle all three readings.
present_status: 2026-11: settled under explicit conventions; intended reading ambiguous.

title: Eliminating a component of a differential system
notes: Two scalar equations are related by a transformation called Bäcklund.
statement: For continuously differentiable scalar coefficients and nowhere-zero \(q_{12}\), eliminating from \((DI+Q)\varphi=0\) gives \([(D+q_{22})q_{12}^{-1}(D+q_{11})-q_{21}]\varphi_1=0\), with \(\varphi_2=-q_{12}^{-1}(D+q_{11})\varphi_1\). Reverse elimination requires \(q_{21}\ne0\).
reconstruction: \ours{} Pivot invertibility and operator order are supplied. An arbitrary linear combination needs a cyclic-coordinate condition.
fate: Classical elimination; the 2005 quasideterminant review, sections 1.2 and 8, gives related noncommutative packaging.
present_status: 2026-11: valid locally under the stated conditions.

title: The constant-coefficient characteristic operator
notes: The scalar operator is the characteristic quadratic.
statement: For constant complex Q, every component of \((DI+Q)\varphi=0\) is annihilated by \(\det(DI+Q)\). The converse requires a cyclic-coordinate condition.
reconstruction: \ours{} The commuting adjugate proves annihilation. For Q=0, f(t)=t solves the scalar second-order equation but cannot be a component of a constant vector solution.
fate: Classical identity; the explicit counterexample excludes an unrestricted converse.

title: Block quasideterminants and the third-order count
notes: Four order-two and thirty-six order-three expressions are mentioned.
statement: If the complementary matrix \(A^{ij}\) is invertible, \(|A|_{ij}=a_{ij}-r_i^{,j}(A^{ij})^{-1}c_j^{,i}\). There are at most \(n^2\) pivot-labelled quasideterminants: four at order two and nine at order three.
reconstruction: Thirty-six might count syntactic expressions, but no convention is specified. Products and inverses must exist.
fate: Gelfand--Retakh 1991, received November 1990; formulas checked in the 2005 review, Example 1.2.3 and Proposition 1.2.6. The notebook establishes 1988 circulation. Earlier 1965-80.9/GP-1965-07 is related, not identical.

title: Noncommutative K-theory and homology
notes: K-theory and homologies are said to arise.
statement: No functor, ring class, homology theory, comparison map or theorem is specified.
reconstruction: Localization and determinant constructions are possible thematic interpretations, not identified intentions.
fate: The 2005 quasideterminant review, section 3, supplies related constructions only.

title: Cayley's two-by-two-by-two hyperdeterminant
notes: The eight-entry determinant is immediately credited to Cayley.
statement: In characteristic zero, the discriminant of \(\det(xA_0+yA_1)\) is Cayley's quartic, up to normalization. Its vanishing detects a geometric singular point of the trilinear form on three projective lines.
reconstruction: The geometric condition is over the algebraic closure; this is not the general-format problem.
fate: Classical construction; GKZ 1989 identifies the projective-dual framework. This item's initial publication check was metadata only.

title: The critical Ising torus partition function
notes: A theta-one numerator and mixed temperature/geometric parameters appear.
statement: For the standard critical zero-field Ising CFT, \(Z=\tfrac12(|\theta_2/\eta|+|\theta_3/\eta|+|\theta_4/\eta|)\), with geometric modulus in the upper half-plane. The odd theta constant at zero vanishes.
reconstruction: Criticality, bulk normalization and boundary sectors are required. This is not an arbitrary finite-lattice or temperature-inversion identity.
fate: Ginsparg, equations 7.16--7.17; DLMF 20.4.1. Lectures 1988, publication 1989.
present_status: 2026-11: established with corrected index and normalization.

title: Theta products and chiral normalization
notes: Nome powers and theta-three/theta-four signs conflict.
statement: For \(q=e^{2\pi i\tau}\), \(\operatorname{Im}\tau>0\), the square-root ratios for indices 2,3,4 are respectively \(\sqrt2q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1+q^n)\), \(q^{-1/48}\prod_{n\ge1}(1+q^{n-1/2})\), and \(q^{-1/48}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^{n-1/2})\). Also \(\eta=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)\).
reconstruction: Branches are positive on the imaginary axis; one nome convention is used.
fate: Ginsparg, equation 7.13; DLMF section 20.4.
present_status: 2026-11: established products; source rows require emendation.

title: Modular transformations of blocks
notes: Block permutations coexist with conflicting periods and group relations.
statement: Use \(S\tau=-1/\tau\), \(T\tau=\tau+1\). Full correlator pairings are monodromy-invariant while blocks may transform projectively. \(S^2=(ST)^3=1\) holds in PSL(2,Z); standard SL(2,Z) lifts give minus identity.
reconstruction: The central quotient, multipliers and cylinder-coordinate convention are distinguished.
fate: Ginsparg, equations 7.14--7.17; Moore--Seiberg 1989 organizes duality matrices.

title: Sewing surfaces and complex moduli
notes: Sewing and the count 3g minus 3 are discussed.
statement: A smooth compact complex curve of genus \(g\ge2\) has local deformation dimension \(3g-3\). Plumbing near a stable nodal curve uses \(uv=t\) together with component moduli. Torus periods are in the upper half-plane modulo SL(2,Z).
reconstruction: These are local descriptions subject to automorphisms; topology alone selects no CFT.
fate: Classical background in Ginsparg, section 10, and Moore--Seiberg 1989.

title: Finite holomorphic factorization in rational CFT
notes: Finitely many left and right blocks are paired.
statement: For a fixed consistent rational chiral theory and admissible labels, finite-dimensional chiral and antichiral block spaces pair through a monodromy-invariant matrix. Finite block dimension does not imply finite state-space dimension.
reconstruction: Rationality, consistency, labels and pairing are supplied; no complete pentagon or hexagon is recorded here.
fate: Partial match to Moore--Seiberg 1988 and 1989. Reports circulated May and August 1988; journal publications followed in October 1988 and June 1989. Abstracts/metadata, not complete proofs, checked.

title: Elliptic functions as parameterized trigonometry
notes: Gelfand calls elliptic functions trigonometry with a parameter.
statement: As Jacobi modulus \(k\to0\), sn tends to sine, cn to cosine, and dn to one, locally away from moving poles; the nome tends to zero.
reconstruction: A specified degeneration illustrates the analogy without defining every elliptic function.
fate: DLMF section 22.5(ii).
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Dehn twists and genus-two relations
notes: Five curves accompany braid, commuting, chain and long-word relations.
statement: Right twists commute for disjoint curves and braid for intersection one. The fourth power of a three-chain product is the product of its boundary twists; an appropriate genus-two embedding identifies these boundary twists.
reconstruction: Orientation and curve labelling are necessary. The handwritten long word is not certified as a complete presentation.
fate: Farb--Margalit was checked at publisher-metadata level; the long relation was not verified from the full book.
present_status: 2026-11: local relations established; long word conditional.

title: Chiral modules and a tentative coproduct
notes: Sector decompositions and contour splitting suggest a coproduct.
statement: Rational full state spaces have left/right sector decompositions with finite nonnegative integer multiplicities. Primitive diagonal Virasoro modes add central charges, so they do not define an ordinary coproduct on a fixed-charge quotient without retaining the central generator.
reconstruction: \ours{} The central-charge obstruction qualifies the contour argument.
fate: Moore--Seiberg 1989 gives a related duality framework; abstract/metadata checked, not the literal coproduct assertion.
present_status: 2026-11: chiral framework established; proposed coproduct schematic.

title: Conformal invariance and Ricci flatness
notes: Conformal invariance is said to imply Ricci flatness.
statement: With no antisymmetric tensor and constant dilaton, the leading metric beta function is \(\beta^G_{\mu\nu}=\alpha'R_{\mu\nu}+O(\alpha'^2)\), up to conventions. Its vanishing imposes Ricci flatness at that order; classical Weyl invariance alone does not.
reconstruction: Field content and perturbative order are supplied; higher corrections change the equations.
fate: Callan et al. 1985; original abstract/front page read, not the full calculation.

title: What replaces space in quantization?
notes: Discrete geometry and polyhedra are suggested; Planck length is written with incorrect units.
statement: No category, observables, quantization map or limiting criterion is fixed. Planck length is approximately \(1.6\times10^{-35}\) metres, equivalently \(1.6\times10^{-33}\) centimetres; that scale does not select a geometry.
reconstruction: No particular discrete or noncommutative theory is adopted as the unique answer.
fate: CODATA 2022 verifies the numerical unit correction.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: An internal CFT replacing compact coordinates
notes: Four coordinate fields and an internal theory supply matter charge twenty-six.
statement: In a critical bosonic string, four free coordinate bosons plus internal central charge twenty-two cancel the bc-ghost charge minus twenty-six. Left/right consistency, modular invariance and BRST conditions are additional requirements.
reconstruction: This is the bosonic, not superstring, charge condition.
fate: Polyakov 1981; Ginsparg--Moore, section 5.2.
present_status: 2026-11: standard construction with further consistency conditions.

title: A functional integral over closed-string fields
notes: Morozov seeks an action for loop functionals.
statement: A bounded reconstruction asks for a gauge-consistent closed bosonic string-field action reproducing worldsheet sewing perturbatively and satisfying the quantum BV master equation.
reconstruction: Ghosts, BRST state space and perturbative scope are supplied; no convergent loop-functional measure is asserted.
fate: Zwiebach, abstract and sections 3--4: June 1992 preprint, 1993 publication. Partial realization of the broader request.
present_status: 2026-11: perturbative action exists; literal measure not thereby defined.

title: Component fields of a string functional
notes: A loop functional is Fourier-expanded in a free parameter sigma.
statement: Expand a string field in a string-state basis with momentum, oscillator, polarization and ghost labels. The embedding itself separately has Fourier modes in sigma. A scalar functional of the whole loop has no free sigma.
reconstruction: The displayed equality conflates two different expansions.
fate: Zwiebach, section 2, verifies the standard component framework without dating its invention to 1992.
present_status: 2026-11: component framework established; literal equality false.

title: The scalar propagator as particle paths
notes: A supposedly free scalar action contains a cubic term.
statement: For \(m>0\), the Euclidean free Green kernel away from the diagonal is \(\int_0^\infty(4\pi T)^{-d/2}e^{-m^2T-|x-y|^2/(4T)}dT\). A free scalar action is quadratic; a nonzero cubic term is an interaction.
reconstruction: Proper-time normalization and Euclidean interpretation replace unrestricted length-integral shorthand.
fate: Ginsparg--Moore, section 5.1; the free/cubic contradiction is elementary.
present_status: 2026-11: classical formula; recorded free-action label false.

title: Smooth worldsheets and interactions
notes: Smooth topology changes are drawn but particles are called free.
statement: Closed-string amplitudes involve marked surfaces, moduli and BRST insertions after gauge fixing. Smooth pair-of-pants surfaces encode splitting or joining in a time slicing. Excluding nonmanifold branch loci therefore does not eliminate interactions.
reconstruction: Smooth topology change is distinguished from singular branching.
fate: Polyakov 1981; Ginsparg--Moore, section 5.2.

title: Removing the square root with an einbein
notes: The mass power and differential are inconsistent.
statement: For positive einbein and a regular Euclidean path, \(S=\tfrac12\int(e^{-1}\dot x^2+m^2e)dt\). If \(m>0\) and velocity is nonzero, stationarity gives \(e=|\dot x|/m\) and \(S=mL\).
reconstruction: \ours{} Factors and mass square are repaired. Quantum equivalence also needs a measure and reparameterization gauge fixing.
fate: Ginsparg--Moore, section 5.1; direct variation checks the repair.

title: The proposed exact auxiliary integral
notes: An integral without contour or limits is equated to a simple exponential.
statement: For \(a,b>0\), \(\int_0^\infty e^{-a\lambda-b/\lambda}d\lambda/\lambda=2K_0(2\sqrt{ab})\). The corresponding positive-exponent integral diverges on this contour.
reconstruction: \ours{} Substitute t=a lambda. \oursComputed{} Quadrature at a=2,b=3 agrees with the corrected Bessel expression.
fate: DLMF equation 10.32.10.
present_status: 2026-11: false as written; corrected integral evaluated.

title: The Polyakov metric integral and area term
notes: Worldsheet metrics replace the einbein; an area exponential is called removable.
statement: The Euclidean Polyakov action uses the worldsheet metric to contract target derivatives. Its formal integral requires diffeomorphism/Weyl treatment, ghosts, anomaly and moduli. The area coupling is a cosmological term whose removal or tuning is model-dependent.
reconstruction: A positive exponent without a contour is not a convergent Euclidean definition.
fate: Polyakov 1981; Ginsparg--Moore, section 5.2.
present_status: 2026-11: standard formalism; universal removal claim false.

title: Background equations from worldsheet invariance
notes: Ricci, Yang--Mills and other equations are attributed to one-loop invariance.
statement: Quantum Weyl/BRST consistency imposes beta-function conditions for specified couplings. Ricci flatness is the leading pure-metric condition with other backgrounds absent or constant. Yang--Mills requires a gauge-background coupling; it does not follow from a metric-only action.
reconstruction: Field content, anomaly and perturbative order are supplied.
fate: Callan et al. 1985 abstract checked; later equations read in Ginsparg--Moore, section 5.2.

title: Matter on a random metric
notes: Scalar fields and an area coupling enter a formal metric integral.
statement: At specified topology this is a Euclidean scalar-matter/random-metric model. Definition requires a diffeomorphism quotient, Weyl-anomaly and zero-mode treatment, and regularization. Susceptibility is parameterized by matter central charge, not necessarily an integer coordinate count.
reconstruction: No continuum measure is constructed from the displayed formal expression.
fate: Polyakov 1981 gives the framework; KPZ 1988 is a separate contemporary result, checked bibliographically.
present_status: 2026-11: standard formal model; realization depends on regime.

title: KPZ susceptibility and central-charge range
notes: The radical, four special charges and the range D at least twenty-six are recorded.
statement: For the usual sphere branch with suitable \(c\le1\), \(\gamma=(c-1-\sqrt{(1-c)(25-c)})/12\). At \(c=-2,0,1/2,1\), the values are \(-1,-1/2,-1/3,0\). The singular free-energy part is intended; c=1 needs logarithms. Radical reality for \(c\ge25\) alone establishes no corresponding physical theory.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} Values checked exactly; topology and branch supplied.
fate: KPZ metadata checked; formula read in Ginsparg--Moore, equation 2.22.
present_status: 2026-11: subcritical formula established; high-charge inference unjustified.

title: Pure-gravity asymptotics and universality
notes: A power law and the base 256/27 are called universal.
statement: Generic pure-gravity coefficients weighted by inverse automorphism group have power \(n^{-7/2}\); rooting contributes a factor proportional to n and yields \(n^{-5/2}\). Exponential growth constants depend on ensemble and coupling. Matter or multicritical weights can change exponents.
reconstruction: The base 256/27 belongs to a specified triangulation convention.
fate: Tutte, equation 8.1; Ginsparg--Moore, sections 6--7.

title: The factorial formula attributed to Tutte
notes: The quotient is labelled by twice k internal vertices and a doubtful final factor.
statement: Tutte's count with three fixed boundary vertices and n internal vertices is \(T_n=2(4n+1)!/((3n+2)!(n+1)!)\). The recorded quotient is \(T_{k-1}\), with power \(k^{-5/2}\) and base \(256/27\). A literal factor \(9^k\) changes the base to \(256/3\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} Specialization and coefficient ratio checked. The alternative reading of the last glyph as g remains open.
fate: Tutte, section 1 and equation 5.11; received 1961, published 1962.
present_status: 2026-11: sequence identified; combined literal count false or incomplete.

title: The graph Gaussian and its zero mode
notes: An adjacency determinant is used without adequate boundary data.
statement: A connected graph Laplacian has a translation zero mode, so the unrestricted Gaussian diverges. Pinning one vertex gives \(\pi^{D(n-1)/2}\det(L_{\rm red})^{-D/2}\). Dirichlet data instead select the internal Laplacian; \(3I-G_{\rm int}\) requires total degree three including boundary edges.
reconstruction: \oursComputed{} For K4, the full determinant is zero and the pinned determinant sixteen.
fate: Finite Gaussian diagonalization; context in Ginsparg--Moore, sections 6--7.
present_status: 2026-11: reduced formula established; source boundary prescription incomplete.

title: Projective space and tautological twists
notes: Projective points are lines; O(-1) has that line as fibre.
statement: For finite-dimensional complex V, use \(0\to O(-1)\to V\otimes O\to Q\to0\). Tensor powers and duals define all O(k).
reconstruction: The line convention fixes later twist signs.
fate: BGG 1978 and Coanda--Trautmann, section 1.3.

title: An exterior module gives a linear complex
notes: Square-zero multiplication yields a bundle, subsequently called a sheaf.
statement: For a finite-dimensional graded exterior module M, \(L(M)^i=O(i)\otimes M_i\), with tautological multiplication differential. Its cohomology sheaves are coherent. Fibre cohomology agrees with specialized sheaf cohomology only under appropriate base-change or constant-rank hypotheses.
reconstruction: Pointwise quotients need not be vector bundles.
fate: BGG 1978; explicit conventions in Coanda--Trautmann, section 1.3.

title: The dimension-one and dimension-two exercise
notes: The requested meaning of the low-dimensional answers is unspecified.
statement: For dimension one, the construction is a finite complex over a point. For dimension two, algebraic bundles on complex P1 split into O(d). For \(d\ge0\), \(0\to O(-1)^d\to O^{d+1}\to O(d)\to0\), and its dual, give bounded constructions of positive and negative twists.
reconstruction: \ours{} This solves a bundle-construction interpretation, not classification of every exterior module.
fate: Grothendieck, Theorem 2.1, supplies splitting.

title: The free exterior module is acyclic
notes: The exterior algebra itself gives zero cohomology.
statement: For \(v\ne0\), choose \(\lambda(v)=1\). Then \(\iota_\lambda(v\wedge\omega)+v\wedge\iota_\lambda\omega=\omega\), proving contractibility.
reconstruction: \ours{} The contracting homotopy supplies a direct proof.
fate: Classical Koszul exactness used by BGG.

title: The incorrect exterior-kernel twist
notes: The raw wedge kernel is identified with a wrongly twisted form bundle.
statement: With the first retained term in degree zero, the kernel is \(O(-1)\otimes\Lambda^{k-1}Q\), for \(1\le k\le\dim V\). Its fibre is \(\ell\wedge\Lambda^{k-1}(V/\ell)\). At k=1 it is O(-1), not O(1).
reconstruction: \ours{} Split off the tautological line. Shifts and dualizations cannot remain implicit.
fate: Coanda--Trautmann, section 1.3, explains related dual Koszul conventions; the correction is direct.

title: The symplectic module and null correlation
notes: The relevant form is annotated symmetric.
statement: For nondegenerate alternating omega on complex V of dimension 2r, \(O(-1)\to V\otimes O\to O(1)\) is a complex because \(\omega(v,v)=0\). The rank-one endpoint maps give the rank \(2r-2\) null-correlation bundle \(v^\perp/\mathbb Cv\).
reconstruction: \ours{} Alternation is essential. A symmetric form gives square-zero multiplication only on its isotropic quadric.
fate: Directly checked example in the BGG framework.
present_status: 2026-11: established after correcting symmetric to alternating.

title: Every projective bundle comes from an exterior module
notes: Degree-zero homology represents every bundle, with other cohomology zero.
statement: For an algebraic vector bundle E on complex P(V), some finite-dimensional graded exterior module has \(\mathcal H^0L(M)=E\) and all other cohomology zero. Presentations are nonunique before stable equivalence.
reconstruction: Finiteness and the sheaf formulation are explicit; local splitting validates the fibre description.
fate: BGG, Theorem 1: Russian 1978, translation 1979. Earlier existence thread GP-1977-11 includes 1977-437.2, 1977-437.11, 1977-438.5 and 1979-468.13.

title: Can derived categories be avoided?
notes: The notes ask this and report S. Gelfand's negative expectation; the questioner is not explicitly identified.
statement: A bounded reading asks for an explicit proof of the bundle theorem without invoking derived equivalence as a black box. No formal class of forbidden arguments is specified.
reconstruction: The operational criterion is supplied; no prohibition on all homological algebra is inferred.
fate: Eisenbud--Floystad--Schreyer, Theorems 4.1 and 6.1; Coanda--Trautmann, Theorem 2.2. These substantially meet the constructive aim without certifying complete categorical elimination. GP-1979-03 and GP-1977-11 are related, not identical.
present_status: 2026-11: constructive forms established; no open obstruction inferred.

title: Graded Clifford normalization
notes: The anticommutator lacks two although unit generators square to h.
statement: Use \(vw+wv=2b(v,w)h\), with central h, so \(v^2=b(v,v)h\). Isotropic multiplication is square-zero. Setting h=1 gives the ordinary Clifford algebra. In positive-definite real dimension three its even part is quaternionic.
reconstruction: \ours{} The factor two, specialization, field and even-part qualification are supplied.
fate: Kapranov, section 4.1; the paper also identifies the 1986 announcement.

title: Kapranov's quadric analogue
notes: The isotropic Clifford complex is said to give an analogous theorem.
statement: For a smooth complex quadric from a nondegenerate form, with dim(V)>3, tautological isotropic multiplication defines a linear complex. Kapranov gives a derived-category description using line and spinor objects and a diagonal resolution. An arbitrary module need not have only one locally free cohomology sheaf.
reconstruction: Smoothness, dimension and cohomological restrictions are supplied.
fate: Kapranov, section 4.1, Propositions 4.6--4.9 and Theorem 4.10; 1988 publication after a 1986 announcement.

title: Cube rotations and S4
notes: Cube motions are called a symmetric group of order four.
statement: Orientation-preserving cube symmetries act faithfully on the four unoriented body diagonals. There are twenty-four rotations, so this action gives S4. The full forty-eight-element symmetry group is S4 times C2.
reconstruction: \ours{} A signed permutation fixing all diagonal lines is plus or minus identity; orientation excludes minus identity. \oursComputed{} Enumeration gives twenty-four distinct diagonal permutations.
fate: The action and order argument solve the classical exercise.
present_status: 2026-11: solved; degree four must replace order four.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Euclidean and symplectic geometry
notes: Both geometries are described as equally legitimate.
statement: Positive-definite symmetric forms define Euclidean geometry; nondegenerate alternating forms define symplectic geometry and require even real dimension.
reconstruction: This clarifies a curricular comparison without asserting equivalence, exclusivity or a global theorem.
fate: Classical linear-algebraic background.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Spin on a mass shell
notes: A nonzero mass hyperboloid is annotated zero rest mass.
statement: For \(m>0,p_0>0\), \(p_0^2-|\mathbf p|^2=m^2\); the SU(2) little group gives spin-j fibre dimension \(2j+1\). Zero mass instead gives the positive null cone and the double cover of E(2); finite helicity requires trivial translation action.
reconstruction: Positive energy and the massive/massless distinction are supplied.
fate: Wigner, sections 6C--D and 7, pp. 189--198; publication 1939.
present_status: 2026-11: classical; the source mass annotation is false.

title: SO(3) on a two-component spinor
notes: The exercise asks for a linear action on complex dimension two.
statement: Every continuous complex two-dimensional SO(3) representation is trivial. Its nontrivial irreducibles have odd dimensions at least three. The defining SU(2) representation descends only projectively to SO(3), since central minus identity acts nontrivially.
reconstruction: \ours{} Continuity and complex linearity distinguish the literal question from the spinor interpretation.
fate: Wigner, section 7A, pp. 193--194.
present_status: 2026-11: solved; nontrivial spin-half uses SU(2) or projective SO(3).

title: Mathematics corresponding to arbitrary spin
notes: Ordinary and super mathematics motivate a broader question; braids are mentioned.
statement: No objects, tensor structure, commutation law, dimension or success criterion fixes the requested framework.
reconstruction: Neither the Poincare classification nor a unique braided-algebra problem is identified with this wording.
fate: Wigner solves a different classification; Dunne, section 2.1, explains planar anyons. Both are thematic.
present_status: 2026-11: target unidentified; no definite open problem inferred.

title: Planar exchange phases
notes: Arbitrary planar phases are contrasted with higher-dimensional statistics.
statement: For at least two identical collision-free points, unordered configuration spaces have fundamental group BN in spatial dimension two and SN in dimensions at least three. Scalar unitary braid characters permit any exchange phase; permutation characters give plus or minus one.
reconstruction: Scalar sectors, spatial dimension and additional spin-statistics assumptions are explicit; nonabelian sectors are not excluded.
fate: Wilczek 1982 fractional-spin paper: primary abstract/metadata checked; higher-dimensional topology follows by general position.

title: Aharonov--Bohm and worldline weights
notes: Exchange and a complete circuit are not distinguished.
statement: A charge encircling flux acquires \(e^{iq\Phi/\hbar}\). Scalar characters can weight homotopy classes of propagators. If exchange phase is z, a full winding gives \(z^2\). Open paths require a reference class or closure.
reconstruction: Charge, endpoint and exchange/winding conventions are supplied.
fate: Wilczek 1982 flux paper; Dunne, equations 19--20, explicitly verifies the factor two.
present_status: 2026-11: established mechanism; source phase conventions incomplete.

title: Chern--Simons versus the Wess--Zumino label
notes: The epsilon A F term is labelled Wess--Zumino.
statement: The three-dimensional abelian epsilon A F density is Chern--Simons. Matter coupling produces flux attachment. Finite Maxwell coupling adds a propagating massive mode, so the action is not purely a linking functional.
reconstruction: An exact topological comparison needs the pure limit; a long-distance comparison needs its approximation stated. Coefficients and global level conditions remain unspecified.

title: Fractional quantum Hall application
notes: The phase mechanism is applied to the Hall effect.
statement: Well-separated quasiparticles in suitable incompressible fractional Hall phases acquire an adiabatic Berry phase with a fractional statistical contribution after background subtraction.
reconstruction: This is not a statement about every Hall excitation; no filling or Hamiltonian is given.

title: The high-temperature application
notes: An abbreviation may mean conductivity or superconductivity; bare names follow.

reconstruction: The abbreviation is unresolved; names alone identify no publication.

title: Witten's Chern--Simons/Jones relation
notes: Morozov reports Witten's recent interpretation.
statement: Compact-group Chern--Simons theory at quantized level assigns Wilson observables to framed links. SU(2) with its defining representation gives Jones evaluations at roots of unity after normalization and framing correction.
reconstruction: This is not the generic scalar Maxwell--Chern--Simons action; formal integration and rigorous realizations are distinguished.
fate: Witten, sections 2 and 4: July 1988 lecture, September 1988 receipt/revision, 1989 publication.

title: A hierarchy of functionals
notes: A hierarchy and first-variation notation are sketched.
statement: Function space, order and equivalence are unspecified. A modern locality theorem needs a definite smooth calculus, additivity and differential hypotheses.
reconstruction: No exact identification of the hierarchy is inferred.

title: Action phases and stationary phase
notes: Action phases motivate classical trajectories and asymptotic integration.
statement: Let \(a\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\) and real smooth phi have exactly one critical point x0 on the support, interior to it, with nonsingular Hessian Q. Then \(\int ae^{iA\phi}=(2\pi/A)^{n/2}a(x_0)e^{iA\phi(x_0)+i\pi\operatorname{sgn}Q/4}/\sqrt{|\det Q|}+O(A^{-n/2-1})\) as \(A\to+\infty\).
reconstruction: The finite-dimensional theorem constructs no continuum path measure.
fate: Feynman, section 4, for action phases; DLMF 2.3 for the asymptotic framework.

title: A cubic-phase integral
notes: The integral is requested at parameter 100000.
reconstruction: \ours{} Substitute u=Ax cubed and integrate the tail twice by parts. Independent incomplete-gamma evaluation corrected an erroneous draft decimal.

title: The particle action and loop amplitude
notes: A path receives an exponential action phase.
statement: For a specified Lagrangian, interval and sufficiently regular path, \(S[q]=\int L(q,\dot q,t)dt\); the formal quantum weight is \(e^{iS/\hbar}\).
reconstruction: A phase factor is distinguished from a constructed continuum measure.
