title: Legendre transformation and phase sign
notes: The Hamiltonian phase omits dt and has the opposite sign.
statement: If \(H=pv-L\), the usual action is \(\int(p\,dq-H\,dt)\). The displayed \(H\,dt-p\,dq\) is its negative.
reconstruction: The missing differential is a faithful source omission; the sign issue is mathematical.
fate: Classical Hamiltonian action, compared with Feynman, section 4.

title: Symplectic area and boundary phase
notes: A filling surface defines a loop phase.
statement: For a loop bounding D, \(e^{i\int_D\omega/\hbar}\) is independent of filling when the relevant periods are in \(2\pi\hbar\mathbb Z\). A global prequantum line bundle requires integral \([\omega/(2\pi\hbar)]\).
reconstruction: Existence and independence of fillings differ; nonbounding loops need holonomy data.
fate: Kostant, Proposition 2.1.1 and section 2.3 in the opened translation.

title: Finsler wave fronts and Legendre correspondence
notes: Gelfand connects wave fronts and Finsler geometry.
statement: For a smooth strongly convex fibre norm F, the derivative of \(F^2/2\) gives the Legendre map on the slit tangent bundle. Positive-definite fibre Hessian gives local invertibility and the dual indicatrix.
reconstruction: Smoothness, strong convexity and exclusion of zero are reconstructed hypotheses.
fate: Classical Legendre geometry; Kostant supplies related Hamiltonian background, not this exact remark.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The independent-metric surface action
notes: Target and worldsheet indices are inconsistent.
statement: For \(X:\Sigma\to M\), the sigma-model action is proportional to \(\int\sqrt{|h|}h^{\alpha\beta}G_{ab}(X)\partial_\alpha X^a\partial_\beta X^b\,d^2x\), with fixed signatures and normalization.
reconstruction: Covariant target indices and consistent coordinates are restored; no random-surface measure is constructed.
fate: Polyakov 1981, equation 6, p. 208; equation 3 is the area functional.

title: A Legendre transformation of surfaces
notes: A surface analogue is requested without a definite target.
statement: One possible first-order construction sets \(p_a^\alpha=\partial L/\partial u_\alpha^a\), \(H=p_a^\alpha u_\alpha^a-L\), locally where the derivative Hessian is invertible.
reconstruction: This possible reconstruction does not uniquely identify the requested transformation or imply global equivalence.
fate: Helein--Kouneiher 2004, sections 1.1 and 2, is thematic only.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Two connections and transgression
notes: The scalar pairing and interpolation formula are incomplete.
statement: For \(a=A_1-A_0\), \(A_t=A_0+ta\), and invariant trace, \(2\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}(a\wedge F_{A_t})dt\) transgresses \(\operatorname{tr}(F_{A_1}^2-F_{A_0}^2)\). Boundary terms likewise require an invariant pairing.
reconstruction: Common extension and period normalization are additional data; boundary flatness guarantees no arbitrary flat extension.
fate: Witten 1984, equations 12--13, gives the earlier extension and integral-level framework.

title: Cayley's quartic from a matrix pencil
notes: A two-by-two-by-two determinant is formed from a quadratic pencil.
statement: For complex two-by-two slices A,B, the discriminant of \(\det(sA+tB)\) is Cayley's quartic up to nonzero scalar and detects a projective singular point of the trilinear form.
reconstruction: Field and scalar ambiguity are explicit.
fate: Classical construction; GKZ 1989, section 5, supplies the Segre framework.

title: Weighted functions on the basic affine space
notes: Unipotent-invariant, torus-equivariant functions realize representations.
statement: For a complex reductive group and a chosen Borel, dominant-weight subspaces of regular functions on the basic affine space give finite-dimensional highest-weight modules, with duals depending on action convention.
reconstruction: Regularity, dominance and left/right action are required; analytic does not mean polynomial.
fate: Serre 1954, section 4, Theorem 4.

title: A horizontal-form complex for the discriminant
notes: A coefficient-dependent complex should have discriminant torsion.
statement: For a smooth projective variety and very ample line bundle, the first-jet Koszul construction, after sufficiently positive twisting and global sections, is acyclic off the discriminant and yields its equation with the specified dual-defect and determinant conventions.
reconstruction: Smoothness, positivity and determinant-line choices are supplied by the precise later theorem.
fate: GKZ 1989, sections 2--3, Propositions 1--3 and Theorem 1; received 13 December 1988.

title: Replacing Young diagrams
notes: An alternative is proposed without a construction.
statement: Replacement objects, equivalence, algorithm and classification target are unspecified.
reconstruction: The slogan is separated from the definite highest-weight and complex constructions.
fate: No unique later theorem was identified.

title: Symmetric powers in small rank
notes: Homogeneous polynomials illustrate SL2 and SL3 representations.
statement: Every finite-dimensional irreducible complex SL2 module is a symmetric power of the defining module. For SL3 these powers cover only one highest-weight ray; general irreducibles have two nonnegative coordinates.
reconstruction: The SL2 classification is not extended to all SL3 modules.
fate: Etingof, Theorem 11.16 and section 27.2, presents the classical results.

title: Classification for symmetric and classical groups
notes: Several representation theories form a pedagogical programme.
statement: Finite-dimensional complex theories use partitions or dominant integral weights with rank, parity and group-form qualifications. This does not classify arbitrary-field or arbitrary infinite-dimensional representations.
reconstruction: Characteristic zero, finite dimension and group forms delimit the programme.
fate: Etingof, sections 25--28 and Theorem 27.3.

title: Gauss factorization on the big cell
notes: The source already says almost every element.
statement: In complex SLn, lower-unipotent, diagonal and upper-unipotent factors give a unique decomposition where the relevant leading principal minors are nonzero. Other elements require other Bruhat cells.
reconstruction: The notebook's qualifier is retained; no global factorization is attributed to it.
fate: Classical Gauss/Bruhat theory; Etingof, section 47.2.

title: Regular functions and SLn characters
notes: Analytic equivariant functions are treated as polynomials.
statement: Use regular algebraic functions with the prescribed invariance and character. SLn exponent vectors differing by a common shift give the same torus character, because the diagonal entries have product one.
reconstruction: Analyticity alone does not imply polynomiality.
fate: Serre, section 4; Etingof, section 27.2.

title: Small modules and pattern bases
notes: Trivial, defining and symmetric-square modules are illustrated.
statement: Degree-zero, one and two homogeneous polynomials realize the corresponding symmetric powers. General irreducibles require all dominant weights; Gelfand--Tsetlin interlacing patterns give an arbitrary-rank basis.
reconstruction: The examples are not exhaustive; action conventions may dualize weights.
fate: Gelfand--Tsetlin 1950, section 3, formula 3, reprint p. 655, visually inspected.

title: Borel--Weil--Bott qualifications
notes: Line bundles and higher cohomology realize representations.
statement: For an integral weight on a complex flag variety, singular shifted weight gives zero cohomology. Otherwise the nonzero degree is the length of the Weyl element taking the shifted weight to dominance; the module depends on the line-bundle convention.
reconstruction: The rho shift, singular case, degree and possible dual are explicit.
fate: Serre, Theorem 4, for Borel--Weil; Bott 1957 for higher cohomology. Bott metadata/abstract, not full theorem, checked.

title: An odd differential determinant
notes: The expression is Psi(z) times a determinant with rows z,dz,dz.
statement: For \(E=\sum z_i\partial_{z_i}\), the exterior-ordered determinant satisfies \(\Psi(z)\det(z;dz;dz)=2\Psi(z)\iota_E(dz_1\wedge dz_2\wedge dz_3)\). It is horizontal because \(\iota_E^2=0\).
reconstruction: \ours{} Anticommuting one-forms make the paired terms add. Closedness and projective descent require further homogeneity hypotheses.
fate: GKZ 1989, sections 3--4, supplies the horizontal-form framework; the local expansion is supplied here.

title: An unexplained rectangular array
notes: A four-by-three array has no complete construction.
statement: The array alone determines no unique minor, resultant, tensor discriminant or determinant complex.
reconstruction: Missing invariance and differential data are not invented.
fate: No unique publication match identified.

title: Noncommutative determinants
notes: A determinant theory over noncommutative coefficients is requested.
statement: A chosen pivot and invertible complementary submatrix define the quasideterminant as pivot minus row times inverse complementary matrix times column. Multiplication order matters and different pivots give different expressions.
reconstruction: This is a precise partial answer; see 1988-753.4.
fate: Gelfand--Retakh 1991; formula read in the 2005 review, Example 1.2.3 and Proposition 1.2.6.
present_status: 2026-11: quasideterminants established; broader programme only partly identified.

title: The determinant equation of singular matrices
notes: The ordinary determinant is characterized by zero locus and degree.
statement: Over an algebraically closed field, singular n-by-n matrices form the irreducible hypersurface det A=0. Every polynomial vanishing there is divisible by det A; minimum nonzero degree is n, with uniqueness up to scalar in that degree.
reconstruction: Finite-field point sets require a different assertion.
fate: Classical determinant example in the GKZ projective-duality setting.

title: Cube monomials in Cayley's quartic
notes: Cube configurations organize hyperdeterminant monomials.
statement: The discriminant of a complex trilinear form on three two-dimensional spaces is Cayley's quartic, equivalently the discriminant of its quadratic matrix-pencil determinant.
reconstruction: The pencil fixes the polynomial up to scalar; the drawing alone does not fix every coefficient.
fate: Classical example; GKZ 1989, section 5.

title: Discriminant as torsion of a finite complex
notes: A section-dependent complex should have discriminant torsion.
statement: Under smooth projective, very ample and sufficiently positive twist hypotheses, the jet-Koszul complex is generically acyclic and its determinant gives the discriminant, with appropriate constant convention for dual defect.
reconstruction: Determinant lines, multiplicities and twists are essential. Regular and logarithmic toric constructions have different outputs.
fate: GKZ dual paper, sections 2--3; Cayley--Koszul paper, sections 4--5, Theorems 4--5. The latter was received June 1989; English translation 1990.

title: Equations and degrees for tensor formats
notes: The all-format hypersurface assertion is too broad.
statement: For a nontrivial complex Segre product, the dual is a hypersurface exactly when every projective dimension is at most the sum of the others. Tensor format two-by-two-by-four violates the condition. Determine equations and degrees in the hypersurface cases.
reconstruction: Class A concerns the equation/degree programme; the existence criterion is earlier.
fate: GKZ, section 6 after Corollary 2, explicitly credits Knop--Menzel 1987 for the criterion.

title: Poincare and Klein disk coordinates
notes: A radial disk-model map is displayed.
statement: On the open unit disk, \(x\mapsto2x/(1+\|x\|^2)\) sends Poincare coordinates to Klein coordinates. The boundary is excluded and metric formulas differ.
reconstruction: The explicit coordinate formula is an editorial reconstruction.
fate: Beltrami 1869 supplies historical context; publication metadata, not the full proof, checked.

title: Binary hyperdeterminant degrees
notes: Two finite sums and a factorial asymptotic are given.
reconstruction: d counts binary factors. \oursComputed{} Independent evaluation agrees for d=2 through 12; testing is not a general proof.
fate: GKZ 1989, section 6.

title: The Gaussian model and analytic torsion
notes: A degenerate quadratic integral is related to torsion.
statement: On a closed oriented three-manifold, after separating zero modes, the Gaussian absolute ratio is \((\det'\Delta_0)^{3/4}/(\det'\Delta_1)^{1/4}=T_{RS}^{1/2}\), with \(T_{RS}=\prod_q(\det'\Delta_q)^{(-1)^{q+1}q/2}\).
reconstruction: Phases, stabilizers and cohomology volumes require additional factors.
fate: Schwarz 1978 metadata/abstract checked; the ratio read in Witten, equation 2.8.

title: The nonabelian Chern--Simons action
notes: A cubic gauge action supplies a topological framework.
statement: With a fixed invariant trace, \(S\propto\int\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A^3)\). On a closed manifold its variation is proportional to \(\int\operatorname{tr}(\delta A\wedge F_A)\), so stationary connections are flat. The exponential requires appropriately quantized level.
reconstruction: Group, bundle and trace conventions are supplied; the formal integral is not a probability measure.
fate: Witten, section 1; July and September 1988 circulation predates this talk.

title: Four-dimensional transgression and level
notes: A curvature integral in four dimensions represents the action.
statement: The derivative of the Chern--Simons form is \(\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)\). Given a bounding four-manifold and bundle extension, the action is defined modulo characteristic periods; allowed levels make its exponential independent of choices.
reconstruction: Existence of the extension is additional data.
fate: Witten, section 1 following equation 1.3.
present_status: 2026-11: established under extension and normalization hypotheses.

title: Surgery and gluing
notes: Cutting and gluing are proposed as a calculation method.
statement: Gluing needs boundary state spaces, their pairing and the gluing map. Surgery additionally needs framing and induced operators.
reconstruction: The abbreviated prescription does not determine every required datum.
fate: Witten, section 4, develops the pre-seminar programme.

title: Wilson loops and framing
notes: A holonomy trace can be misread as the action.
statement: For a representation R and closed curve K, \(W_R(K;A)=\operatorname{Tr}_R\operatorname{Hol}_K(A)\) is an inserted observable. Its quantum invariant requires framing and normalization.
reconstruction: The observable is distinguished from S(A), with representation and path ordering explicit.
fate: Witten, equations 1.5--1.7 and section 2.

title: The matrix Euler equation
notes: A matrix Euler analogue uses a commutator.
statement: For smooth finite-dimensional \(\dot\Omega=[\Omega,h]\), every \(\operatorname{tr}(\Omega^k)\) is conserved. In a Hamiltonian interpretation h is the trace gradient with a declared Lie--Poisson convention.
reconstruction: Trace cyclicity proves conservation; signs and pairing are explicit.
fate: Arnold 1966; Zakharov, section 6.

title: Matrix Clebsch variables and word traces
notes: A commutator representation gives integrals of words.
statement: Set \(\Omega=[p,q]\), \(\dot p=[p,h]\), \(\dot q=[q,h]\). Then \(\dot\Omega=[\Omega,h]\), and traces of all words in p,q are conserved. Trace differentiation gives \(H_p=[q,h]\), \(H_q=[h,p]\), hence \(\dot p=-H_q,\dot q=H_p\).
reconstruction: Signs are consistent; no global parametrization of every orbit is asserted.
fate: Zakharov, section 6; submitted 2 November 1988, published 1989.

title: Hamiltonian vector fields and their bracket
notes: The resulting scalar potential has an inconsistent derivative index.
statement: With \(\{f,g\}=f_xg_y-f_yg_x\) and \(A_f=\{f,\cdot\}\), Jacobi gives \([A_f,A_g]=A_{\{f,g\}}\). Potentials are defined modulo constants.
reconstruction: No extra x derivative belongs on the new potential.
fate: Zakharov, sections 1--2; Arnold's geometric setting.

title: Euler energy and vorticity
notes: Stream function, energy and vorticity are linked by integration by parts.
statement: For smooth periodic zero-mean \(\Omega=\Delta\Psi\), \(H=\tfrac12\int|\nabla\Psi|^2=-\tfrac12\int\Psi\Omega\), \(H_\Omega=-\Psi\), and \(\Omega_t=\{\Omega,\Psi\}\) in the declared convention.
reconstruction: Boundary conditions and the removed Laplacian zero mode are essential.
fate: Zakharov, section 1; Arnold 1966.

title: Scalar Clebsch variables and canonical signs
notes: Canonical signs and the historical date require correction.
statement: Assume smooth single-valued periodic labels with \(\Omega=\{\lambda,\mu\}\). Then \(H_\lambda=\{\Psi,\mu\}\), \(H_\mu=-\{\Psi,\lambda\}\), and \(\lambda_t=H_\mu,\mu_t=-H_\lambda\) advect the labels and induce Euler.
reconstruction: Global labels are assumed; the unexplained 1844 attribution is not adopted.
fate: Clebsch 1857/1859; precise setup in Zakharov, section 2.

title: Brackets of advected scalars
notes: Repeated brackets produce transported quantities.
statement: If smooth f,g satisfy \(f_t+\{\Psi,f\}=g_t+\{\Psi,g\}=0\), then \(\{f,g\}_t+\{\Psi,\{f,g\}\}=0\), by Jacobi.
reconstruction: The assertion does not cover arbitrary weak solutions.
fate: Classical identity used in Zakharov, section 2.

title: Integrating functions of transported quantities
notes: Functions of advected labels are integrated.
statement: For smooth incompressible transport, integrals of smooth functions of finitely many advected scalars are conserved when finite and with vanishing boundary flux, for example on a compact boundaryless area domain.
reconstruction: Label-dependent quantities need not descend to vorticity-only functionals.
fate: Standard transport conservation, Zakharov, section 2.
present_status: 2026-11: established under boundary and regularity hypotheses.

title: The iterated-bracket integral family
notes: Repeated label brackets enlarge the conserved family.
statement: Close advected Clebsch labels under spatial Poisson brackets, then integrate smooth functions of finitely many resulting scalars under the stated boundary conditions. These are conserved functionals on the enlarged label phase space.
reconstruction: Conservation does not imply completeness, involution or descent to Eulerian phase space.
fate: Zakharov, sections 2--3, gives the exact construction.

title: The grade-zero label algebra
notes: A label derivative index is inconsistent.
statement: For \(J_F^0=\int F(\lambda,\mu)\) and \(\{I,J\}_{can}=\int(I_\lambda J_\mu-I_\mu J_\lambda)\), \(\{J_F^0,J_G^0\}_{can}=J_{\langle F,G\rangle}^0\), where \(\langle F,G\rangle=F_\lambda G_\mu-F_\mu G_\lambda\).
reconstruction: The label-plane bracket is distinct from the spatial bracket.
fate: Zakharov, section 3.

title: The current bracket and exceptional grade
notes: The coefficient and exceptional denominator need correction.
statement: For \(J_F^n=\int F(\lambda,\mu)\Omega^n\), nonnegative n,m and \(n+m\ne1\), \(\{J_F^n,J_G^m\}_{can}=-(n-1)(m-1)J_{\langle F,G\rangle}^{n+m}/(n+m-1)\). For global smooth periodic labels, \(J_F^1=0\).
reconstruction: The exceptional case is separate. Multivalued labels or boundaries can change grade-one vanishing; rescale by 1 minus n only away from that grade.
fate: Zakharov, equation 3.7, p. 192; leading minus sign visually checked.

title: A Witt subalgebra
notes: The integral algebra is compared with circle vector fields.
statement: On \(\lambda\ne0\), \(F_n=\lambda^{n+1}\mu\), \(n\in\mathbb Z\), satisfies \(\langle F_m,F_n\rangle=(m-n)F_{m+n}\). The integral representation can have a kernel.
reconstruction: Negative powers require the domain restriction; the entire current algebra is not Witt.
fate: Classical Witt relation, compared in Zakharov, section 3.

title: Completeness of the geometric integrals
notes: The integrals and fixed lambda are considered reconstruction data.
statement: They do not determine generic mu: area-preserving spatial relabelings generated by f(lambda) fix lambda and the geometric integrals but change mu, infinitesimally by f-prime(lambda) times Omega.
reconstruction: This is incompleteness of the specified family, not universal nonintegrability of Euler.
fate: Exact obstruction in Zakharov, sections 2--3; submitted 2 November 1988.

title: A quartic Fourier Hamiltonian
notes: Quadratic vorticity energy becomes quartic in label coefficients.
statement: For a real even multiplier f on permitted modes, \(H_f=\tfrac12\sum_k f(k)|\Omega_k|^2\), with fixed Fourier normalization and \(\Omega=\{\lambda,\mu\}\), is quartic in the label coefficients.
reconstruction: Reality, convergence or formal truncation, zero modes and normalization must be specified.
fate: Zakharov, section 5.

title: Ratio multipliers and a formal Lax pair
notes: A ratio of linear Fourier forms is singled out.
statement: For commuting directional derivatives, set \(h=D_\beta^{-1}D_\alpha\Omega\), \(L=\zeta D_\beta+A_\Omega\), \(M=\partial_t-\zeta D_\alpha-A_h\). Then \([L,M]=A_{-\Omega_t-\{\Omega,h\}+\zeta(D_\alpha\Omega-D_\beta h)}\).
reconstruction: The reconstruction fixes signs. Resonant modes, small divisors and inverse domains require control; deleting modes need not be invariant.
fate: Zakharov, section 5, matches the formal programme.
present_status: 2026-11: formal compatibility identified; no global analytic integrability inferred.

title: A numerical chaos programme
notes: Numerical exploration is suggested.
statement: No truncation, parameter set, method, observable or quantitative chaos criterion defines a reproducible experiment.
reconstruction: No verified chaotic trajectory or universal nonintegrability follows.
fate: Zakharov, section 5, matches the proposal, not a uniquely completed experiment.

title: An ambiguous three-dimensional vector formula
notes: The expression is [A,curl B] minus [B,curl A], with undefined bracket.
statement: If brackets mean cross products, take \(A=e_1,B=\cos y\,e_1\). Both inputs are divergence free, but the expression has divergence \(-\cos y\). Separately, a global \(v^\flat=d\phi+\lambda d\mu\) on a closed three-manifold has zero helicity since \(v^\flat\wedge dv^\flat=d(\phi d\lambda\wedge d\mu)\).
reconstruction: \ours{} These conditional counterchecks retain the glyph ambiguity; single-valuedness and no boundary are essential.
fate: Clebsch 1859 supports the local scalar construction, not a universal global reading.

title: Projective duality and the cubic cusp
notes: Tangent hyperplanes and a cubic graph illustrate duality.
statement: The dual is the closure of hyperplanes tangent at smooth points. A linear Pr in Pn has dual dimension n minus r minus one when nonempty. For \(y=x^3\), tangent parameters \(k=3t^2,b=-2t^3\) satisfy \(27b^2=4k^3\).
reconstruction: The local tangent relation is not a global convex Legendre--Fenchel transform.
fate: Classical projective duality; GKZ, section 1.

title: Polarity of lp balls
notes: Dual norms are illustrated by conjugate exponents.
statement: In finite-dimensional real space with standard pairing, the polar of the unit lp ball is the unit lq ball for conjugate exponents, including one and infinity. Convex norm polarity requires p at least one.
reconstruction: Pairing, endpoints and convex range are explicit.
fate: Classical Holder duality; Figiel supplies related normed-space context.

title: An almost circular cube section
notes: A nearly circular central two-dimensional section is requested.
statement: The plane parametrized by \((a\cos(j\pi/n)+b\sin(j\pi/n))_{j=0}^{n-1}\) has induced cube norm between \(\cos(\pi/(2n))\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\) and \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\). Distortion tends to one.
reconstruction: \ours{} Every unoriented direction is within pi/(2n) of a sample. This is not the distinct four-dimensional cube-section question.
fate: Classical Dvoretzky special case; Figiel, p. 297. Related occurrences: 1964-45.1 and 1976-416.4.

title: The Segre hypersurface criterion
notes: Format inequalities characterize existence.
statement: For a nontrivial complex Segre product, the dual is a hypersurface iff \(\ell_i\le\sum_{j\ne i}\ell_j\) for every i, where each ell is tensor side length minus one.
reconstruction: The all-zero point case is excluded; a higher-codimension dual has no single discriminant equation.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Corollary 2 and following sentence explicitly credit Knop--Menzel 1987. The original earlier theorem was not obtained.

title: The alternating degree sum
notes: The sign exponent and product scopes are ambiguous.
statement: For nonzero ell, with \(s=\sum k_i\), \(N(\ell)=\sum_{0\le k_i\le\ell_i}(-1)^{\sum(\ell_i-k_i)}[(s+1)\prod_i\binom{s}{k_i}\binom{s+1+\ell_i-k_i}{\ell_i-k_i}-s\prod_i\binom{s-1}{k_i}\binom{s+\ell_i-k_i}{\ell_i-k_i}]\). The second term is zero at s=0; N means degree or zero.
reconstruction: Both binomials belong inside each product. \oursComputed{} Generating-series and jet-Chern comparisons agree on 333 tuples; this supports restoration, not an unambiguous glyph reading or general proof.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Theorem 2, supplies the degree theory.
present_status: 2026-11: restored formula independently checked on the stated finite range.

title: Leshchiner's degree generating series
notes: The inverse-square series is attributed to Leshchiner.
statement: For d variables and elementary symmetric polynomials e, \(\sum_{\ell_i\ge0}N(\ell)x^\ell=(1-\sum_{k=2}^d(k-1)e_k(x))^{-2}\). For nonzero ell use degree or zero; \(N(0,\ldots,0)=1\) is a formal convention.
reconstruction: The constant is not a degree-one projective dual of a point.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Theorem 2.
speaker: Leshchiner

title: Kapranov's positive partition sum
notes: Margin feasibility alone is used to infer triangle inequalities.
statement: For nonempty partition lambda, \(N(\lambda)=\sum_{|\mu|=|\lambda|,\,m_1=m_2}\frac{(m_1+1)!\prod_{i\ge2}(i-1)^{m_i-m_{i+1}}}{\prod_{i\ge1}(m_i-m_{i+1})!}M(\mu',\lambda)\), where M counts zero-one matrices with those margins. Standard dominance gives \(\lambda\preceq\mu\).
reconstruction: \ours{} Rows 110,101,100 have column sums (3,1,1): positive M alone does not imply triangle inequalities. The restriction m1=m2 is essential; opposite dominance notation remains a possible convention.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Corollary 1.
present_status: 2026-11: restricted formula established; unqualified inference false.
speaker: M. M. Kapranov

title: Zelevinsky's boundary-format degree
notes: A factorial formula and the two-by-three-by-four example are proposed.
statement: For nontrivial boundary format \(\ell_1=\sum_{i>1}\ell_i\), \(N=(\ell_1+1)!/\prod_{i>1}\ell_i!\). Tensor sides two,three,four give reordered projective dimensions three,two,one, hence degree twelve.
reconstruction: Subtract one from tensor side lengths first; the example supplies no complete polynomial or precise minimality assertion.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Corollary 3(a).
speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky

title: Degenerate forms and the Segre dual
notes: Degeneracy is simultaneous vanishing of all partial contractions.
statement: Over C, for nonzero finite-dimensional Vi and at least two factors, a nonzero multilinear A is degenerate iff there are nonzero vi such that each contraction leaving one slot free vanishes. Equivalently, its projective class belongs to the Segre dual. A hypersurface dual has an irreducible equation unique up to scalar.
reconstruction: Field and projective conventions are supplied; uncertain coefficient strokes define no new operation.
fate: Classical definition recalled in GKZ, section 5.
present_status: 2026-11: established; an equation requires codimension one.

title: Formats admitting a hyperdeterminant
notes: The largest dimension parameter must not exceed the sum of the others.
statement: For complex \(\prod_i\mathbb P^{\ell_i}\), with nonnegative integral ell, at least two factors and positive total dimension, the dual is a hypersurface iff \(\ell_i\le\sum_{j\ne i}\ell_j\) for all i. Two factors therefore require a square matrix.
reconstruction: The all-zero format has empty projective dual; the degree-one scalar convention is affine.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Corollary 2 and following attribution to Knop--Menzel 1987.

title: Boundary-format degree
notes: Boundary equality is followed by a factorial degree.
statement: For tensor sides \(\ell_i+1\), with \(\ell_1=\sum_{i>1}\ell_i\), the reduced hyperdeterminant has total degree \((\ell_1+1)!/\prod_{i>1}\ell_i!\). The all-zero case uses the affine scalar convention.
reconstruction: Reduced equation and total degree are explicit.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Corollary 3(a); received December 1988, published 1989.

title: Generating series for all degrees
notes: A reciprocal square uses incorrectly repeated elementary-symmetric indices.
statement: With degree-or-zero N and affine scalar convention N(0)=1, \(\sum_{\ell_i\ge0}N(\ell)x^\ell=(1-\sum_{i=2}^d(i-1)e_i(x))^{-2}\), where \(e_i=\sum_{k_1<\cdots<k_i}x_{k_1}\cdots x_{k_i}\). This is a formal power-series identity.
reconstruction: Distinct indices and the finite upper limit are restored.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Theorem 2, credits the derivation jointly with Leshchiner.

title: Degrees from zero-one matrix margins
notes: Binary matrices with specified margins are proposed.
statement: Let M(rho,ell) count labelled zero-one matrices, and let rho contain ni copies of i, i=2,...,d, with \(r=\sum n_i\). Then \(N(\ell)=\sum_{n_i\ge0}(r+1)!\prod_i(i-1)^{n_i}M(\rho,\ell)/\prod_i n_i!\). Only \(\sum i n_i=\sum\ell_j\) contributes; the empty matrix contributes one.
reconstruction: This equivalent coefficient expansion uses \(M=[x^\ell]\prod e_i^{n_i}\); it is not a verbatim formula from the notes.
fate: GKZ, section 6, Corollary 1.

title: A Cayley complex detecting the discriminant
notes: A finite section-linear complex fails acyclicity on the discriminant.
statement: For smooth irreducible complex projective X and very ample L, a section has a singular zero divisor iff its first jet vanishes. After sufficient positive twisting, the jet-Koszul construction gives a finite section-linear complex whose determinant yields the hypersurface discriminant with its prescribed exponent and determinant-line convention.
reconstruction: Arbitrary linear complexes do not qualify; positivity and hypersurface hypotheses are essential.
fate: GKZ dual paper, sections 2 and 5; toric variants distinguished in the Cayley--Koszul paper, Theorems 1--7.

title: Determinant lines and rational torsion
notes: Alternating determinant lines and minor ratios are described.
statement: For a finite-dimensional finite complex, \(\det C^\bullet=\bigotimes_i(\det C^i)^{(-1)^i}\) identifies, with fixed sign convention, with the corresponding determinant of cohomology. Acyclicity trivializes the line. Compatible nonzero minors in chosen bases express its torsion on acyclic charts.
reconstruction: Finite dimension, ordered bases and nonzero chart minors are essential.
fate: Knudsen--Mumford, section 1, introduction identified; discriminant application read in GKZ, section 2.

title: The four-term complex for a matrix determinant
notes: Dimensions one, four, seven and four and a minor quotient are indicated.
statement: For \(X=\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\), \(L=O(1,1)\), zero twist, \(C_i=H^0(X,\Omega_X^i(i))\oplus H^0(X,\Omega_X^{i-1}(i))\) has dimensions 1,4,7,4. The section is bilinear and its discriminant is the ordinary two-by-two determinant.
reconstruction: P1 cohomology gives the dimensions; absent differential matrices prevent checking the specific minor quotient.
fate: GKZ, section 3, Theorem 1 and corollary; section 5, Proposition 5.
present_status: 2026-11: construction established; notebook matrices only partly matched.

title: The two-row differential-form complex
notes: A local plus sign conflicts with square-zero composition.
statement: For complex Segre X, \(L=O(1,\ldots,1)\), \(C_i^{(m)}=H^0(\Omega_X^i(i+m))\oplus H^0(\Omega_X^{i-1}(i+m))\). With ordinary left wedge multiplication, use \(D_\ell\omega=(A d\omega-\ell dA\wedge\omega)/(\ell+1)\). The plus rule instead gives \(D_{\ell+1}D_\ell\omega=2A dA\wedge d\omega/((\ell+1)(\ell+2))\).
reconstruction: \ours{} This local calculation preserves the diplomatic plus and does not invent missing global conventions.
fate: GKZ, section 3, product before Proposition 3 and Theorem 1.
present_status: 2026-11: construction established; local sign needs emendation.
speaker: M. M. Kapranov

title: Highest-weight orbit embeddings
notes: A highest-weight orbit carries a complete embedding.
statement: For connected complex semisimple algebraic G and irreducible finite-dimensional highest-weight W, the orbit of a highest-weight line in P(W) is closed, equal to G/P for its stabilizer. With induced L, \(H^0(G/P,L)\simeq W^*\), giving the complete linear system.
reconstruction: The field and dual convention are explicit.
fate: Standard homogeneous example recalled in GKZ, section 1.

title: Toric closures and shared Segre examples
notes: Characters define an orbit closure; Segre varieties connect the examples.
statement: For integral characters chi, the closure of \(t\mapsto[t^{\chi_1}:\cdots:t^{\chi_N}]\) is projective toric, possibly nonnormal. Configurations can be homogenized into an affine hyperplane. Segre products are both homogeneous and toric.
reconstruction: This lists shared examples, not a classification. Principal determinant and dual discriminant differ.
fate: GKZ dual paper, section 1; subsequent Cayley--Koszul developments.

title: Unassigned Betti-number jumps
notes: An unheaded fragment emphasizes jumps on a representation space.
statement: The acting object, representation space, cohomology theory, degree and varying family are unspecified.
reconstruction: Physical placement establishes neither attribution nor a character-variety interpretation.
fate: No exact target was identified; this is not evidence of an undeveloped theorem.
speaker: Unattributed annotation

title: Unassigned Jones-polynomial heuristic
notes: The polynomial is described as a scheme for computing prior invariants.
statement: No invariants, category, grading or testable equality are specified.
reconstruction: Khovanov homology and finite-type invariants are not retrospectively inserted.
fate: Later thematic theories do not establish an exact match.
speaker: Unattributed annotation

title: Four roughly equivalent representation settings
notes: Modular, quantum-group, loop-group and Schubert settings are compared.
statement: This is a programme relating character questions and geometry. Groups, characteristics, root orders, levels, categories and functors are absent; unrestricted equivalence is not a precise theorem.
reconstruction: No characteristic bound or particular comparison theorem is supplied.
fate: Lusztig 1989 is a thematic chapter. Williamson's abstract addresses precise modular bounds, not this unspecified programme.
present_status: 2026-11: the intended restricted theorem cannot be identified.

title: Rank-one reflection and a Weyl-module sequence
notes: Polynomial-labelled modules have Weyl-module arrows for an unrestricted weight.
statement: For algebraically closed characteristic p>0, G=SL2 and \(p\le\ell\le2p-2\), put \(\ell'=2p-2-\ell\). Then \(0\to L(\ell')\to\Delta(\ell)\to L(\ell)\to0\) is nonsplit. For \(\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(k^2)=\nabla(\ell)\), factors reverse. Weights zero through p minus one give simple modules.
reconstruction: Group, interval and Weyl/induced distinction are reconstructed.
fate: Doty--Henke, section 1, Lemma 1.1 and proof; recalls classical structure.

title: Five affine lines and six bounded regions
notes: The drawing says always six bounded regions.
statement: Five real affine lines with no parallel pair and no triple concurrence have sixteen regions, six bounded and ten unbounded. Equivalently designate a line at infinity among six general-position projective lines.
reconstruction: Five parallel lines disprove an unrestricted reading.
fate: Elementary arrangement count; Zaslavsky's 1974 thesis/1975 publication verified through author metadata, full memoir unread.

title: The quartic-root elliptic integral
notes: An elliptic integral is written beside the line drawing.
statement: For distinct complex a,b,c,d, the smooth projective model of \(y^2=(x-a)(x-b)(x-c)(x-d)\) double-covers P1 with four branch points and has genus one. A base point makes it elliptic; dx/y extends holomorphically across branch points and both points above infinity.
reconstruction: Distinct roots and compact smooth model are supplied; no integral evaluation is claimed.
fate: Hain, section 5.1, Proposition 5.2 and Appendix A, Exercise 78; quartic coordinates reconstructed.
present_status: 2026-11: curve and differential identified; relation to drawing unknown.

title: The missing bridge from lines to the integral
notes: A doubtful instruction accompanies the integral.
statement: No map from six lines to four branch values, incidence condition or period identity is specified.
reconstruction: Neither Pascal's theorem nor a double-plane K3 construction is inserted.
fate: No exact connecting statement identified.

title: The compact complex K3 condition
notes: Simple connectedness and trivial holomorphic two-form bundle are stated.
statement: For a connected compact smooth complex surface X, \(\pi_1(X)=0\) and \(K_X\simeq O_X\) characterize a complex K3 surface. Triviality means a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic two-form.
reconstruction: Compactness and dimension two are essential: complex affine two-space satisfies the written conditions but is not K3.
fate: Huybrechts, Chapter 1, section 3 and simple-connectedness discussion.

title: The common smooth manifold of K3 surfaces
notes: All K3 surfaces are said to be diffeomorphic.
statement: Any two compact complex K3 surfaces are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic as smooth real four-manifolds with their complex orientations.
reconstruction: This asserts neither biholomorphism nor realization of every exotic smooth structure.
fate: Kodaira's deformation-equivalence result; Huybrechts, Chapter 1, Remark 3.6 and Chapter 7, Theorem 1.1.

title: Kummer quotient and sixteen nodes
notes: T/(2x=0) is explained verbally by x identified with minus x.
statement: For a full lattice in complex two-space, T modulo the involution minus one has sixteen ordinary double points, at T[2], locally complex two-space modulo plus/minus one. Its minimal resolution is K3. Quotient by translations by T[2] is instead a smooth torus.
reconstruction: The verbal involution fixes the intended quotient; projectivity is unnecessary.
fate: Huybrechts, Chapter 1, Examples 1.3(iii) and 3.3.

title: The Plücker quadric and a second quadric
notes: The separate drawing has no K3 label.
statement: Over C, Gr(2,4) in P5 is \(p_{12}p_{34}-p_{13}p_{24}+p_{14}p_{23}=0\). A transverse intersection with another quadric is a smooth degree-four threefold with \(K=O(-2)\).
reconstruction: Dimension and adjunction are editorial clarification; no missing third quadric is invented.
fate: Classical calculation; the K3 example in Huybrechts, Chapter 1, Example 1.3(ii), uses three quadrics.

title: KZ monodromy and braid representations
notes: A comparison is attributed to Kohno and another person.
statement: For a nonexceptional complex simple Lie algebra with vector representation, and for sl2 with a finite-dimensional irreducible, KZ monodromy agrees with the corresponding normalized quantum R-matrix representation as a meromorphic parameter family, with the theorem's special-parameter qualifications.
reconstruction: This does not compare arbitrary braid matrices.
fate: Kohno 1987, Theorems 1.2.8 and 2.2.4, Remark 1.3.14; later formal comparison in Drinfeld, Proposition 3.16.
present_status: 2026-11: qualified comparison established; handwritten attribution incomplete.

title: Hopf algebra and antipode
notes: Algebra, coproduct, counit and antipode are recalled.
statement: A Hopf algebra has unital associative A, unital algebra maps Delta and epsilon, coassociativity and counit identities, and \(m(S\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=\eta\varepsilon=m(\mathrm{id}\otimes S)\Delta\). Drinfeld additionally requires bijective S, giving left and right duals for finite-dimensional modules.
reconstruction: Counit and antipode identities complete the shorthand.
fate: Drinfeld's ICM report, section 1, pp. 798--800; lecture 1986, proceedings 1987.
present_status: 2026-11: classical definition with stated source convention.

title: Quasibialgebra and quasiantipode
notes: An associator weakens coassociativity; antipode data are abbreviated.
statement: Require normalized invertible Phi with \((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Delta=\Phi(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta\Phi^{-1}\) and \((\mathrm{id}^{\otimes2}\otimes\Delta)\Phi(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}^{\otimes2})\Phi=(1\otimes\Phi)(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Phi(\Phi\otimes1)\). Quasi-Hopf additionally requires a quasiantipode S,alpha,beta satisfying the two twisted antipode equations and the two Phi-normalization equations.
reconstruction: Alpha and beta need not individually be invertible. The complete axioms are those in the cited equations; associator data alone define only a quasibialgebra.
fate: Drinfeld, equations 1.1--1.4 and 1.17--1.19; received 23 May 1989, Russian 1989, English 1990.

title: The module associator and pentagon
notes: Diagrams compare bracketings of modules.
statement: For left modules, Delta defines tensor action, epsilon the unit, and Phi acts as \((U\otimes V)\otimes W\to U\otimes(V\otimes W)\). Quasiassociativity gives A-linearity; the pentagon equates the two four-module composites. Quasiantipode data give duality for finite-dimensional modules.
reconstruction: Associator direction and finite-dimensional rigidity are explicit.
fate: Drinfeld, section 1 following equations 1.4 and 1.17--1.19.

title: The R-matrix and hexagons
notes: An opposite coproduct and incomplete tensor-slot label occur.
statement: For normalized invertible R, \(\Delta^{op}(a)=R\Delta(a)R^{-1}\), with opposite equal to flip after Delta. The hexagons are \((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})R=\Phi_{312}R_{13}\Phi_{132}^{-1}R_{23}\Phi_{123}\) and \((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)R=\Phi_{231}^{-1}R_{13}\Phi_{213}R_{12}\Phi_{123}^{-1}\).
reconstruction: Tensor permutations are explicit; incomplete 31 becomes 231. Flip after R-action gives the braiding.
fate: Drinfeld, equations 3.8--3.9.

title: Gelfand's duality question
notes: Gelfand asks for the dual structure.
statement: For finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf A, H=A-star has coproduct dual to multiplication and multiplication dual to Delta. With \(\omega(p,q,r)=\langle p\otimes q\otimes r,\Phi^{-1}\rangle\), \(\sum((p_1q_1)r_1)\omega(p_2,q_2,r_2)=\sum\omega(p_1,q_1,r_1)p_2(q_2r_2)\), with dual pentagon and antipode data.
reconstruction: An infinite full dual need not coproduct into its ordinary tensor square; restriction or topology is necessary.
fate: Schauenburg, sections 2--3; preprint 2002, publication 2004.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Twisting the structure
notes: A gauge element F transforms the tensors.
statement: For invertible counit-normalized F, \(\Delta_F=F\Delta F^{-1}\), \(\Phi_F=(1\otimes F)(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)F\,\Phi(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})F^{-1}(F^{-1}\otimes1)\), and \(R_F=F_{21}RF^{-1}\). If \(F=\sum f^1\otimes f^2\), \(F^{-1}=\sum g^1\otimes g^2\), use \(\alpha_F=\sum S(g^1)\alpha g^2\), \(\beta_F=\sum f^1\beta S(f^2)\).
reconstruction: Formally require F congruent to one modulo h and completed tensor products; product order matters.
fate: Drinfeld, equations 1.11--1.12, quasiantipode discussion and equation 3.11.

title: The invariant-tensor construction
notes: An enveloping algebra has ordinary coproduct and exponential R.
statement: For a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra g and invariant \(t\in S^2g\), use U(g)[[h]], ordinary coproduct/counit and \(R=e^{ht/2}\). An invariant associator in the completed third tensor power gives a quasitriangular quasi-Hopf structure.
reconstruction: Neither semisimplicity nor nondegeneracy of t is required; no numerical-h convergence is asserted.
fate: Drinfeld, Theorem 3.15 and the following KZ construction.

title: The regularized KZ associator
notes: Solutions normalized at singular endpoints are compared.
statement: For \(R=e^{ht/2}\), set \(\kappa=h/(2\pi i)\) and \(G'=\kappa(t_{12}/z+t_{23}/(z-1))G\). On the real interval choose \(G_0=H_0z^{\kappa t_{12}}\), \(G_1=H_1(1-z)^{\kappa t_{23}}\), with regular endpoint factors equal to one. Then \(\Phi=G_1^{-1}G_0\) is constant.
reconstruction: Regularization, transition direction and parameter rescaling are supplied; multipoint flatness gives coherence identities.
fate: Drinfeld, equation 3.25 and following argument.

title: Formal quasitriangular QUE structures up to twist
notes: The shorthand describes all relevant structures as classical-data constructions.
statement: In characteristic zero restrict to h-adically complete topologically free quasitriangular quasi-Hopf deformations reducing to an ordinary enveloping Hopf algebra, with R and Phi congruent to one. Up to normalized twist and isomorphism, the framework uses a formal Lie-algebra deformation, invariant symmetric tensor and universal associator.
reconstruction: The classical pair may depend on h; this does not classify arbitrary quasi-Hopf algebras.
fate: Drinfeld, Introduction and Theorem 3.15, explicitly postpones part of the proof.
present_status: 2026-11: qualified framework established; notebook scope only partly matched.

title: Gelfand's hypergeometric interpretation
notes: Gelfand connects the construction with hypergeometric functions.
statement: On a finite-dimensional representation, the reduced three-point KZ equation is a matrix Fuchsian system with regular singularities at zero, one and infinity; solutions and transitions have iterated-integral descriptions.
reconstruction: This supports a generalized hypergeometric interpretation, not reduction of every system to a scalar Gauss equation.
fate: Kohno, sections 1.1--1.3; compare Drinfeld's KZ construction.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The finite Ising partition function and sign
notes: Partition sum and ferromagnetic Hamiltonian have incompatible signs.
statement: For finite undirected G, count every edge once. With \(H=-\sum_{e=uv}J_e\sigma_u\sigma_v\), \(Z=\sum_\sigma e^{-\beta H}=\sum_\sigma e^{\beta\sum_eJ_e\sigma_u\sigma_v}\). Ferromagnetism requires nonnegative couplings; summing both orientations requires one-half.
reconstruction: Finite volume and compatible edge/sign conventions are supplied.
fate: Duminil-Copin, section 2.2; Kulske, section 2.

title: Thermodynamic pressure and boundary independence
notes: Khanin recommends finite containers and normalized log Z.
statement: For translation-invariant finite-range lattice Ising interactions with fixed finite couplings and field, normalized log partition functions converge along boxes and van Hove sequences. Boundary changes involving a subextensive number of bounded interactions preserve the limit, since \(|\log Z_1-\log Z_2|\le\beta\sup|H_1-H_2|\). Physical free-energy density is minus pressure divided by beta.
reconstruction: Extensive boundary modifications and irregular non-van-Hove limits are excluded.
fate: Duminil-Copin, section 2.2, equation 2.5, states the box limit; van Hove is the standard extension.
speaker: K. M. Khanin

title: Sources generate spin correlations
notes: A magnetic field generates correlations by differentiation.
statement: For finite \(Z(\beta,\eta)=\sum_\sigma e^{\beta\sum J_e\sigma_u\sigma_v+\sum\eta_x\sigma_x}\), \(\partial_{\eta_x}\log Z=\langle\sigma_x\rangle\), and second derivatives give connected covariance. Derivatives of Z divided by Z give ordinary products.
reconstruction: Dimensionless source differs from a physical field; a positive Hamiltonian field term h gives eta equal to minus beta h.
fate: Finite differentiation; conventions in Kulske, section 2, and Duminil-Copin, section 2.2.
present_status: 2026-11: exact finite identities; limiting derivatives need estimates.

title: What contours determine
notes: Spins are called uniquely determined by nonintersecting contours.
statement: On a connected finite graph, the disagreement set is a cut and determines spins only up to global reversal. A reference spin fixes this. Planar dual disagreement edges form an even subgraph, possibly with degree-four vertices.
reconstruction: Resolved disjoint polygons require a pairing convention and boundary/exterior-face rules.
fate: Duminil-Copin, section 3.1 and Figure 4; finite multiplicity proved in the development.
present_status: 2026-11: qualified correspondence exact; unrestricted uniqueness false.

title: Normalization of the low-temperature sum
notes: A bare contour sum uses lambda equal to exp(-2 beta).
statement: For free zero-field spins on a graph with c components and distinct-cut set C, \(Z=2^ce^{\beta\sum J_e}\sum_{D\in C}\prod_{e\in D}e^{-2\beta J_e}\). Connected unit couplings give \(2e^{\beta|E|}\sum_D\lambda^{|D|}\).
reconstruction: Pinning one spin per component removes the multiplicity; exterior boundary conditions can also change admissible cuts.
fate: Contour context in Duminil-Copin, section 3.1; factors proved in the development.

title: A planar Gaussian Grassmann representation
notes: The local matrix C and boundary choices are incomplete.
statement: Finite planar Ising polynomials admit Pfaffian representations after graph, orientation, boundary and prefactor choices. For even antisymmetric K, with \(\int d\psi_n\cdots d\psi_1\,\psi_1\cdots\psi_n=1\), \(\int d\psi_n\cdots d\psi_1 e^{\psi^TK\psi/2}=\operatorname{Pf}K\).
reconstruction: The incomplete C does not specify a unique matrix identity. Covariance additionally depends on action and insertion order.
fate: Dotsenko--Polyakov checked bibliographically; readable correspondence in Cimasoni, section 4, Proposition 4.6.
present_status: 2026-11: planar method established; local notebook match partial.

title: The unspecified C and gamma-five correspondence
notes: C is related to gamma-five equal to sigma-one sigma-two.
statement: For ordinary Pauli matrices, \(\sigma_1\sigma_2=i\sigma_3\) squares to minus one. Hermitian chirality squaring to one is \(-i\sigma_1\sigma_2\), up to sign.
reconstruction: Without Clifford convention, C and a limiting map, the correspondence is not a determinate continuum assertion.
fate: The identified Dotsenko--Polyakov chapter was unavailable in full; metadata cannot supply the missing map.

title: Pauli projectors for lattice steps
notes: Hopping factors use half the identity plus a Pauli contraction.
statement: For a real unit vector alpha, \(P_\alpha=(I+\alpha\cdot\sigma)/2\) has rank one, \(P_\alpha^2=P_\alpha\), and \(P_\alpha P_{-\alpha}=0\).
reconstruction: Unit length and Pauli conventions are supplied; the full action's contractions remain unspecified.
fate: Elementary Pauli algebra; exact conventions in the cited chapter were not checked from full text.

title: Kac--Ward phases and directed walks
notes: Turning phases weight fermionic walks.
statement: For a finite loop-free straight-edge planar graph, assign undirected weights \(x_e=x_{-e}\). Set \(T_{e,e'}=x_e e^{i\angle(e,e')/2}\) for consecutive nonbacktracking directed edges, otherwise zero. With turning angles between minus pi and pi, \(\det(I-T)=(\sum_{\partial F=\varnothing}\prod_{e\in F}x_e)^2\).
reconstruction: The formal resolvent sums walks; analytic convergence requires spectral radius below one. Primal weights are tanh(beta J); low-temperature weights belong on the appropriate dual graph.
fate: Cimasoni, Theorem 2.1, planar example and Corollary 2.2.
present_status: 2026-11: finite identity and formal expansion established.

title: Berezin integration and the Pfaffian
notes: One-variable integration extracts the linear coefficient.
statement: Over characteristic zero, Grassmann generators anticommute. Fix \(\int d\psi_n\cdots d\psi_1\,\psi_1\cdots\psi_n=1\). For even n and antisymmetric K, the Gaussian integral is Pf(K), with \(\operatorname{Pf}(K)^2=\det K\).
reconstruction: Measure order matters and can change the sign.
fate: Berezin metadata/contents checked; Pfaffian application read in Cimasoni, section 4.

title: Fateev--Zamolodchikov parafermions
notes: The 1985 ZhETF paper is cited for a proposed extension.
statement: The two-dimensional ZN parafermionic CFT has currents of dimensions \(k(N-k)/N\), for 1 through N minus one, and central charge \(2(N-1)/(N+2)\). N=2 gives Ising. These fields are not ordinary lattice Grassmann generators.
reconstruction: No parafermionic extension of the three-dimensional action is specified.
fate: Zamolodchikov--Fateev, equations 2.13 and 3.14; received March 1985, published August 1985.
present_status: 2026-11: cited CFT established; application remains a suggestion.

title: Specific heat and connected energy covariance
notes: Connectedness, volume and the distinction between a sum and its term are omitted.
statement: For finite spins with beta-independent H, \(\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}(H)=\sum_{x,y}\operatorname{Cov}(e_x,e_y)\) when H is the sum of local energies. Translation-invariant couplings and Gibbs measure reduce this to volume times \(\sum_x\operatorname{Cov}(e_x,e_0)\). Specific heat per site is beta squared times variance divided by volume.
reconstruction: The power-law ansatz concerns the unsummed connected correlator; limiting differentiation needs estimates.
fate: Proved in the development; centered energy appears in Duminil-Copin, section 8.4.

title: Hyperscaling and the energy dimension
notes: The ratio formula for alpha is stated.
statement: Assume \(y_t=d-\Delta_\varepsilon>0\), \(\nu=1/y_t\), and hyperscaling \(2-\alpha=d\nu\). Then \(\alpha=(d-2\Delta_\varepsilon)/(d-\Delta_\varepsilon)\).
reconstruction: This proves no lattice scaling hypothesis. Dangerous irrelevant variables, marginal logarithms and regular backgrounds require qualification; two-dimensional alpha zero allows logarithmic heat capacity.
fate: Duminil-Copin, section 4.2; Kulske, section 3.

title: The schematic quartic Grassmann action
notes: Quadratic edge and quartic face terms use incomplete C/M coefficients.
statement: The recoverable claim is a local Grassmann representation on incidence flags, with quadratic local and quartic face terms producing admissible surface weights after normalization. A unique identity needs the cell complex, boundaries, generator order, every coefficient and prefactor.
reconstruction: Those missing data are explicit; a quartic action is not Gaussian and gives no automatic determinant formula.
fate: Dotsenko--Polyakov 1988 predates the talk; identity/pages checked only bibliographically, coefficients unread.
present_status: 2026-11: precursor identified; exact local formula partly verified.

title: The three-dimensional surface sum
notes: Lambda to area is summed over closed surfaces in real three-space.
statement: For a finite cubic-lattice system with plus exterior and unit ferromagnetic couplings, disagreement bonds give admissible dual-plaquette mod-two boundaries. Their area counts disagreements, and the normalized polynomial sums exp(-2 beta area).
reconstruction: Restore the ground-state factor, component multiplicities where appropriate, boundary conditions and periodic homology constraints. Arbitrary smooth surfaces are not the indexing set; touching and branching matter.
fate: Dotsenko--Polyakov metadata; readable surface treatment in Iqbal--McGreevy, sections 2.1--2.2.
present_status: 2026-11: finite expansion exact; no continuum measure follows alone.

title: Marked energy insertions and a string picture
notes: Marked places are linked by a closed fermionic-string description.
statement: For a finite admissible surface polynomial \(\widehat Z=\sum_S\lambda^{A(S)}\), first and second derivatives of log Z with respect to log lambda give mean area and its variance. Local sources generate connected marked-plaquette correlations.
reconstruction: Surface slices suggest loops but define no string Hilbert space, fermionic sign rule or continuum worldsheet action.
fate: Dotsenko 1987 and Dotsenko--Polyakov 1988 are bibliographic precursors only; operator identities unread.
present_status: 2026-11: finite differentiation exact; continuum string construction unspecified.

title: The three-dimensional Ising continuum problem
notes: The closing instruction asks to solve the continuum problem.
statement: The direct question seeks a continuum description and critical thermal behaviour. A stronger reconstruction fixes the critical zero-field nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic model on Z3 and asks for convergence of normalized smeared spin and centered energy fields, with identified correlation scaling and justified thermal relations.
reconstruction: Topology, normalization, full-sequence convergence and moment control are editorial additions. The development proves preparatory finite identities only.
fate: Conditional bootstrap, deformed Hamiltonians and gapped-phase effective strings do not establish this target; Duminil-Copin section 8.4 separates bootstrap data from lattice convergence.
present_status: 2026-11: no checked primary proof of the target found. The complete 2026 exponent-certification claim was not independently audited; exponent bounds alone are not field convergence.
worth: A finite audit is worthwhile because normalization, admissibility and connectedness must be correct. It claims neither novelty nor a new partial continuum solution.
